records.context: A spaCR project is a folder of derived data.  ``merged/`` came from raw images, ``measurements.db`` came from ``merged/``, the model came from the extracted image regions the database indexes, and the hit list came from the model.  The files themselves do not record these links, so without a registry a result cannot be checked against its inputs: after Mask is executed again with a different diameter, every downstream number is out of date and nothing marks it.
records.label: spacr.artifacts#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: A spaCR project is a folder of derived data.  ``merged/`` came from raw images, ``measurements.db`` came from ``merged/``, the model came from the crops the database indexes, and the hit list came from the model.  The files themselves do not record these links, so without a registry a result cannot be checked against its inputs: after Mask is re-run with a different diameter, every downstream number is out of date and nothing marks it.
records.translation: Un proyecto de spaCR es una carpeta de datos derivados.  ``merged/`` procede de las imágenes brutas, ``measurements.db`` procede de ``merged/``, el modelo procede de los recortes que indexa la base de datos y la lista de aciertos procede del modelo.  Los propios archivos no registran estos vínculos, por lo que sin un registro un resultado no puede comprobarse frente a sus entradas: después de volver a ejecutar Mask con otro diámetro, todos los números posteriores quedan desactualizados y nada lo señala.

records.context: Storage is SQLite — ``artifacts.db`` in the project root, one row per artifact plus one edge row per input — because two Measure workers, a GUI and a batch runner can all be touching a project at once, and a pickle cannot survive that.  Writes go through :func:`spacr.database_concurrency.transaction` with an explicit lock budget, which is also why nothing here does its own retry arithmetic.
records.label: spacr.artifacts#8
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Storage is SQLite — ``artifacts.db`` in the project root, one row per artifact plus one edge row per input — because two Measure workers, a GUI and a batch runner can all be touching a project at once, and a pickle cannot survive that.  Writes go through :func:`spacr.database_concurrency.transaction` with an explicit lock budget, which is also why nothing here does its own retry arithmetic.
records.translation: El almacenamiento es SQLite (``artifacts.db`` en la raíz del proyecto, una fila por artefacto más una fila de arista por cada entrada), porque dos procesos de trabajo de Measure, una GUI y un ejecutor por lotes pueden estar accediendo a la vez a un proyecto, y un pickle no lo resistiría.  Las escrituras pasan por :func:`spacr.database_concurrency.transaction` con un presupuesto de bloqueo explícito, que es también la razón por la que nada aquí hace sus propios cálculos de reintentos.

records.source: One SQLite file, opened per operation and closed again: Measure workers, the GUI and a batch runner all register into the same project, and a connection held open across a whole run is a lock held across a whole run. Writes go through :func:`spacr.database_concurrency.transaction` with an explicit lock budget, so a second registration arriving mid-write waits rather than failing.
records.translation: Un único archivo SQLite, que se abre en cada operación y se vuelve a cerrar: los procesos de trabajo de Measure, la GUI y un ejecutor por lotes registran todos en el mismo proyecto, y una conexión abierta durante toda una ejecución es un bloqueo mantenido durante toda una ejecución. Las escrituras pasan por :func:`spacr.database_concurrency.transaction` con un presupuesto de bloqueo explícito, de modo que un segundo registro que llegue a mitad de una escritura espera en lugar de fallar.

records.context: A regular file is hashed end to end while it is small enough to be worth it, and above ``full_hash_limit`` from its size plus its first and last megabyte — enough to notice a rewritten database without spending minutes of I/O at the end of every processing session. A folder is fingerprinted from its file inventory: each file's relative path, size and modification time, in sorted order. Symlinks are skipped — linked files are ignored and linked subfolders are not descended into — so a folder of links fingerprints as empty.
records.label: spacr.artifacts.content_fingerprint#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: A regular file is hashed end to end while it is small enough to be worth it, and above ``full_hash_limit`` from its size plus its first and last megabyte — enough to notice a rewritten database without spending minutes of I/O at the end of every run. A folder is fingerprinted from its file inventory: each file's relative path, size and modification time, in sorted order. Symlinks are skipped — linked files are ignored and linked subfolders are not descended into — so a folder of links fingerprints as empty.
records.translation: Un archivo normal se resume de principio a fin mientras sea lo bastante pequeño como para que merezca la pena y, por encima de ``full_hash_limit``, a partir de su tamaño más su primer y último megabyte, lo suficiente para detectar una base de datos reescrita sin gastar minutos de I/O al final de cada ejecución. La huella de una carpeta se calcula a partir de su inventario de archivos: la ruta relativa, el tamaño y la hora de modificación de cada archivo, en orden. Los enlaces simbólicos se omiten (los archivos enlazados se ignoran y no se desciende a las subcarpetas enlazadas), de modo que una carpeta de enlaces tiene la huella de una carpeta vacía.

records.context: A queued job **is** a ``spacr-run`` invocation. Nothing here re-implements module dispatch or settings loading: :mod:`spacr.cli` owns the module registry, the settings loader, the ``--set`` coercion and the exit-code contract (0 ok, 1 the module raised, 2 bad arguments or settings), and this module drives it. The software job list's own result is a :class:`spacr.errors.RunLedger`, stamped next to the software job list file, and each job's :func:`spacr.errors.read_run_status` stamp is read back so a job that exited 0 having silently skipped 40 fields is reported as *partial* rather than as a success.

records.source: A queued job **is** a ``spacr-run`` invocation. Nothing here re-implements module dispatch or settings loading: :mod:`spacr.cli` owns the module registry, the settings loader, the ``--set`` coercion and the exit-code contract (0 ok, 1 the module raised, 2 bad arguments or settings), and this module drives it. The queue's own result is a :class:`spacr.errors.RunLedger`, stamped next to the queue file, and each job's :func:`spacr.errors.read_run_status` stamp is read back so a job that exited 0 having silently skipped 40 fields is reported as *partial* rather than as a success.
records.translation: Un trabajo en cola **es** una invocación de ``spacr-run``. Nada aquí vuelve a implementar el despacho de módulos ni la carga de la configuración: :mod:`spacr.cli` es dueño del registro de módulos, del cargador de configuración, de la conversión de ``--set`` y del contrato de códigos de salida (0 correcto, 1 el módulo generó una excepción, 2 argumentos o configuración erróneos), y este módulo lo controla. El resultado propio de la cola es un :class:`spacr.errors.RunLedger`, estampado junto al archivo de la cola, y el sello :func:`spacr.errors.read_run_status` de cada trabajo se vuelve a leer, de modo que un trabajo que terminó con 0 tras omitir en silencio 40 campos de imagen se notifica como *parcial* y no como un éxito.

records.context: **State is persisted after every transition, atomically.** A machine that reboots while processing the software job list is resumed with :func:`resume_queue`, not restarted. The file is written to a temp name and ``os.replace``\ d, so a crash cannot leave a truncated work list file.
records.label: spacr.batch#6
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **State is persisted after every transition, atomically.** A machine that reboots mid-queue is resumed with :func:`resume_queue`, not restarted. The file is written to a temp name and ``os.replace``\ d, so a crash cannot leave a truncated queue file.
records.translation: **El estado se conserva tras cada transición, de forma atómica.** Una máquina que se reinicia a mitad de la cola se reanuda con :func:`resume_queue`, no se vuelve a empezar. El archivo se escribe con un nombre temporal y se coloca con ``os.replace``, de modo que un fallo no puede dejar un archivo de cola truncado.

records.context: Jobs that already succeeded are left alone. Jobs that were ``not_run`` (the software job list halted before reaching them) or still ``pending`` are executed. Failed and skipped jobs stay as they are unless ``retry_failed`` is set.

records.source: Jobs that already succeeded are left alone. Jobs that were ``not_run`` (the queue halted before reaching them) or still ``pending`` are run. A job that was ``running`` when the machine went down is reset and run again. For Mask, Measure, and Format Converter jobs the rerun receives ``resume=True`` automatically, so their verified field checkpoints are reused instead of repeating the whole plate. Failed and skipped jobs stay as they are unless ``retry_failed`` is set.
records.translation: Los trabajos que ya se completaron correctamente se dejan intactos. Se ejecutan los trabajos que estaban en ``not_run`` (la cola se detuvo antes de llegar a ellos) o todavía en ``pending``. Un trabajo que estaba en ``running`` cuando la máquina se apagó se restablece y se vuelve a ejecutar. Para los trabajos de Mask, Measure y Format Converter, la nueva ejecución recibe ``resume=True`` automáticamente, de modo que se reutilizan sus puntos de control de campos verificados en lugar de repetir toda la placa. Los trabajos fallidos y omitidos siguen como están salvo que se establezca ``retry_failed``.

For ``prob`` and ``easy`` a missing scores file is reported: it falls back to ``value`` with a notice naming both places it looked; a scores file that leaves some waiting fields unscored says how many; and where the scores came from is printed. Those warnings, and the one that says progress is being written back to the external tool's record beside the folder, are kept on the queue as :attr:`CurationQueue.notices` for the editor to show.
records.translation: Las probabilidades solo se leen para los órdenes que las usan, de modo que ``name`` y ``value`` no leen ningún archivo de puntuaciones; ``uncertain`` lee en su lugar ``curate_uncertainty.csv``. Para ``prob`` y ``easy`` se notifica la ausencia del archivo de puntuaciones: se recurre a ``value`` con un aviso que nombra los dos lugares en los que se buscó; un archivo de puntuaciones que deja sin puntuar algunos campos pendientes indica cuántos; y se imprime de dónde proceden las puntuaciones. Esas advertencias, y la que indica que el progreso se está escribiendo en el registro de la herramienta externa junto a la carpeta, se conservan en la cola como :attr:`CurationQueue.notices` para que el editor las muestre.

records.translation: QC a nivel de placa: detecta efectos de borde y gradientes por filas o columnas en los valores de los pocillos.

records.context: The outer ring of a microtitre laboratory microplate evaporates faster, sits at a different temperature and is handled differently from the interior. A microplate sample position in row A or column 24 that reads three sigma from the laboratory microplate mean is therefore much more likely to be an artefact of *where it sits* than of what is in it.
records.label: spacr.plate_qc#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The outer ring of a microtitre plate evaporates faster, sits at a different temperature and is handled differently from the interior. A well in row A or column 24 that reads three sigma from the plate mean is therefore much more likely to be an artefact of *where it sits* than of what is in it.
records.translation: El anillo exterior de una placa de microtitulación se evapora más deprisa, está a una temperatura distinta y se manipula de forma diferente que el interior. Por ello, un pocillo de la fila A o de la columna 24 que se aleja tres sigmas de la media de la placa tiene muchas más probabilidades de ser un artefacto de *dónde está* que de lo que contiene.

records.context: **The laboratory microplate format is inferred, never assumed.** 6/12/24/48/96/384/1536 are recognised from the observed row and column labels, and the ring geometry uses the *nominal* grid of the inferred format. A screen that only used rows A-H of a 384 laboratory microplate does not get row H promoted to "edge" just because nothing was pipetted below it.
records.label: spacr.plate_qc#10
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **The plate format is inferred, never assumed.** 6/12/24/48/96/384/1536 are recognised from the observed row and column labels, and the ring geometry uses the *nominal* grid of the inferred format. A screen that only used rows A-H of a 384 plate does not get row H promoted to "edge" just because nothing was pipetted below it.
records.translation: **El formato de la placa se infiere, nunca se supone.** 6/12/24/48/96/384/1536 se reconocen a partir de las etiquetas de filas y columnas observadas, y la geometría de anillos usa la cuadrícula *nominal* del formato inferido. Un cribado que solo usó las filas A-H de una placa de 384 no hace que la fila H se convierta en "edge" solo porque no se pipeteó nada por debajo de ella.

records.context: Statistical choices
records.label: spacr.plate_qc#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Statistical choices
records.translation: Decisiones estadísticas

records.context: **Rank tests, not t-tests.** Per-microplate sample position aggregates of object measurements are routinely skewed and heavy-tailed — a microplate sample position with three enormous cells is not a normal deviate. The ring comparison is a two-sided Mann-Whitney U; the gradient test is Spearman. Neither assumes a shape.
records.label: spacr.plate_qc#5
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Rank tests, not t-tests.** Per-well aggregates of object measurements are routinely skewed and heavy-tailed — a well with three enormous cells is not a normal deviate. The ring comparison is a two-sided Mann-Whitney U; the gradient test is Spearman. Neither assumes a shape.
records.translation: **Pruebas de rangos, no pruebas t.** Los agregados por pocillo de mediciones de objetos son habitualmente asimétricos y de cola pesada: un pocillo con tres células enormes no es una desviación normal. La comparación de anillos es una U de Mann-Whitney bilateral; la prueba de gradiente es la de Spearman. Ninguna supone una forma.

records.context: **Effect size leads, p-value follows.** With 384 microplate sample positions, almost any systematic drift clears p < 0.05; that fact carries no information. Every comparison therefore reports the median difference, the difference as a percentage of the interior median, *and* Cliff's delta — a rank-based standardised effect in [-1, 1] read straight off the same U statistic (``δ = 2U/n₁n₂ − 1``). Detection requires both a small p **and** an effect size above :data:`DEFAULT_MIN_EFFECT`, so a significant but 0.4 % difference is not reported as an edge effect.
records.label: spacr.plate_qc#6
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Effect size leads, p-value follows.** With 384 wells, almost any systematic drift clears p < 0.05; that fact carries no information. Every comparison therefore reports the median difference, the difference as a percentage of the interior median, *and* Cliff's delta — a rank-based standardised effect in [-1, 1] read straight off the same U statistic (``δ = 2U/n₁n₂ − 1``). Detection requires both a small p **and** an effect size above :data:`DEFAULT_MIN_EFFECT`, so a significant but 0.4 % difference is not reported as an edge effect.
records.translation: **El tamaño del efecto va primero y el p-value después.** Con 384 pocillos, casi cualquier deriva sistemática supera p < 0.05; ese hecho no aporta información. Por ello, cada comparación informa de la diferencia de medianas, de la diferencia como porcentaje de la mediana del interior *y* de la delta de Cliff, un efecto estandarizado basado en rangos en [-1, 1] que se obtiene directamente del mismo estadístico U (``δ = 2U/n₁n₂ − 1``). La detección exige a la vez un p pequeño **y** un tamaño del efecto superior a :data:`DEFAULT_MIN_EFFECT`, de modo que una diferencia significativa pero del 0.4 % no se notifica como efecto de borde.

records.context: **Evaporation is not a step function.** The profile walks inward ring by ring (outermost = ring 0), comparing each against the laboratory microplate core, so a gradient that reaches two microplate sample positions in is visible instead of being averaged into "the interior".
records.label: spacr.plate_qc#7
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Evaporation is not a step function.** The profile walks inward ring by ring (outermost = ring 0), comparing each against the plate core, so a gradient that reaches two wells in is visible instead of being averaged into "the interior".
records.translation: **La evaporación no es una función escalón.** El perfil avanza hacia dentro anillo a anillo (el más externo = anillo 0), comparando cada uno con el núcleo de la placa, de modo que un gradiente que penetra dos pocillos es visible en lugar de quedar promediado en "the interior".

records.context: **A gradient is not an edge effect.** An incubator or laboratory microplate-reader gradient runs *across* the laboratory microplate; evaporation runs *around* it. A linear column gradient leaves the outer ring with the same median as the interior (it collects both the high and the low end), so the ring test stays quiet while Spearman on the column index fires. Both are computed, both are reported, and :attr:`EdgeEffectReport.dominant` names which one better explains the laboratory microplate.
records.label: spacr.plate_qc#8
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **A gradient is not an edge effect.** An incubator or plate-reader gradient runs *across* the plate; evaporation runs *around* it. A linear column gradient leaves the outer ring with the same median as the interior (it collects both the high and the low end), so the ring test stays quiet while Spearman on the column index fires. Both are computed, both are reported, and :attr:`EdgeEffectReport.dominant` names which one better explains the plate.
records.translation: **Un gradiente no es un efecto de borde.** Un gradiente de incubadora o de lector de placas recorre la placa *de un lado a otro*; la evaporación la recorre *alrededor*. Un gradiente lineal por columnas deja al anillo exterior con la misma mediana que el interior (recoge tanto el extremo alto como el bajo), de modo que la prueba de anillos no detecta nada mientras que la de Spearman sobre el índice de columna sí. Ambas se calculan, ambas se notifican, y :attr:`EdgeEffectReport.dominant` indica cuál explica mejor la placa.

records.context: The outer ring is compared against everything inside it with a two-sided Mann-Whitney U — rank-based, because per-microplate sample position aggregates of object measurements are skewed often enough that a t-test would be testing its own assumptions rather than the laboratory microplate. records.label: spacr.plate_qc.detect_edge_effect#1

records.source: The outer ring is compared against everything inside it with a two-sided Mann-Whitney U — rank-based, because per-well aggregates of object measurements are skewed often enough that a t-test would be testing its own assumptions rather than the plate. The accompanying Cliff's delta comes off the same U statistic, so effect size and p-value cannot disagree about which comparison was made.
records.translation: El anillo exterior se compara con todo lo que hay dentro de él mediante una U de Mann-Whitney bilateral, basada en rangos porque los agregados por pocillo de mediciones de objetos son asimétricos con la frecuencia suficiente como para que una prueba t estuviera evaluando sus propios supuestos y no la placa. La delta de Cliff que la acompaña se obtiene del mismo estadístico U, de modo que el tamaño del efecto y el p-value no pueden discrepar sobre qué comparación se hizo.

records.source: Row and column gradients are tested separately with Spearman on the well index. This is what keeps a plate-reader or incubator gradient from being reported as an edge effect: a linear gradient across the plate leaves the outer ring straddling both extremes, so its median matches the interior and the ring test correctly stays quiet.
records.translation: Los gradientes por filas y por columnas se evalúan por separado con la prueba de Spearman sobre el índice del pocillo. Esto es lo que impide que un gradiente de lector de placas o de incubadora se notifique como efecto de borde: un gradiente lineal a lo largo de la placa deja el anillo exterior abarcando ambos extremos, de modo que su mediana coincide con la del interior y la prueba de anillos, correctamente, no detecta nada.

records.context: **Existing rows are removed prior to inserting replacements.** The measurement workflow calls ``to_sql(if_exists='append')`` to append rows. Measuring a field again would create a duplicate of each object rather than replace the old rows. This makes ``count_cell`` twice as large and biases the mean for each well. Removing old rows prior to another measurement makes the operation safe to repeat.
records.label: spacr.resume.clear_field_rows#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **This is the delete-before-insert.** Measure appends (``to_sql(if_exists='append')``), so re-running a field that already wrote rows adds a second copy of every object rather than replacing the first. Downstream, ``count_cell`` doubles, per-well means are computed over the doubled population, and nothing in the artifact says so. Calling this immediately before re-measuring a field is what makes a resume idempotent.
records.translation: **Este es el borrado previo a la inserción.** Measure añade filas (``to_sql(if_exists='append')``), de modo que volver a ejecutar un campo que ya escribió filas añade una segunda copia de cada objeto en lugar de sustituir la primera. Más adelante, ``count_cell`` se duplica, las medias por pocillo se calculan sobre la población duplicada y nada en el artefacto lo indica. Llamar a esta función justo antes de volver a medir un campo es lo que hace que una reanudación sea idempotente.

records.context: **All or nothing.** Every table is deleted from inside one ``BEGIN IMMEDIATE`` … ``COMMIT``. If any statement fails — a missing table, a trigger, a lock — the transaction is rolled back and the database is left exactly as it was. A half-cleared field would be worse than an uncleared one.
records.label: spacr.resume.clear_field_rows#3

records.source: **All or nothing.** Every table is deleted from inside one ``BEGIN IMMEDIATE`` … ``COMMIT``. If any statement fails — a missing table, a trigger, a lock — the transaction is rolled back and the database is left exactly as it was. A half-cleared field would be worse than an uncleared one.
records.translation: **Todo o nada.** Todas las tablas se borran dentro de un único ``BEGIN IMMEDIATE`` … ``COMMIT``. Si cualquier sentencia falla (una tabla ausente, un disparador, un bloqueo), la transacción se revierte y la base de datos queda exactamente como estaba. Un campo borrado a medias sería peor que uno sin borrar.

records.context: **Keyed on the field, not on its name.** The WHERE clause is equality over ``plateID``/``rowID``/``columnID``/``fieldID``, so clearing ``f1`` cannot touch ``f10``–``f19`` the way a ``LIKE 'plate1_A01_f1%'`` would. A table missing any of the four raises rather than running a broader delete.
records.label: spacr.resume.clear_field_rows#4

records.source: **Keyed on the field, not on its name.** The WHERE clause is equality over ``plateID``/``rowID``/``columnID``/``fieldID``, so clearing ``f1`` cannot touch ``f10``–``f19`` the way a ``LIKE 'plate1_A01_f1%'`` would. A table missing any of the four raises rather than running a broader delete.
records.translation: **Indexado por el campo, no por su nombre.** La cláusula WHERE es una igualdad sobre ``plateID``/``rowID``/``columnID``/``fieldID``, de modo que borrar ``f1`` no puede tocar ``f10``–``f19``, como sí haría un ``LIKE 'plate1_A01_f1%'``. Una tabla a la que le falte cualquiera de las cuatro genera una excepción en lugar de ejecutar un borrado más amplio.

records.context: **Only measure's own tables.** Every table is checked against :data:`MEASURE_OWNED_TABLES` before anything is deleted, and one that is not on it aborts the whole call. ``measurements.db`` is shared — ``conversion_map``, ``align_coordinates`` and ``foreign_*`` live there and carry the same four identifier columns so that they join — and clearing a field out of those destroys the only record of how the project's files were named and registered.
records.label: spacr.resume.clear_field_rows#5

records.source: **Only measure's own tables.** Every table is checked against :data:`MEASURE_OWNED_TABLES` before anything is deleted, and one that is not on it aborts the whole call. ``measurements.db`` is shared — ``conversion_map``, ``align_coordinates`` and ``foreign_*`` live there and carry the same four key columns so that they join — and clearing a field out of those destroys the only record of how the project's files were named and registered.
records.translation: **Solo las tablas propias de measure.** Cada tabla se comprueba frente a :data:`MEASURE_OWNED_TABLES` antes de borrar nada, y una que no esté en ella anula toda la llamada. ``measurements.db`` es compartida (``conversion_map``, ``align_coordinates`` y ``foreign_*`` residen allí y llevan las mismas cuatro columnas de clave para poder unirse), y borrar un campo de esas tablas destruye el único registro de cómo se nombraron y registraron los archivos del proyecto.

records.context: **Only rows measure itself wrote.** Owned by name is not owned in fact: in a project built by ``foreign.run_import`` the rows in ``cell`` are the import's, sitting under spaCR's own metadata columns in a table that is on the allow-list. Every DELETE is therefore narrowed by :func:`measure_rows_clause`, which is true only for rows holding a value in a column the importer never wrote. Clearing a field takes measure's rows for that field and leaves the import's — in the same table, in the same statement.

records.source: **Only rows measure itself wrote.** Owned by name is not owned in fact: in a project built by ``foreign.run_import`` the rows in ``cell`` are the import's, sitting under spaCR's own metadata columns in a table that is on the allow-list. Every DELETE is therefore narrowed by :func:`measure_rows_clause`, which is true only for rows holding a value in a column the importer never wrote. Clearing a field takes measure's rows for that field and leaves the import's — in the same table, in the same statement.
records.translation: **Solo las filas que escribió el propio measure.** Ser propietario por nombre no es serlo de hecho: en un proyecto construido mediante ``foreign.run_import``, las filas de ``cell`` son de la importación y se encuentran bajo las columnas de metadatos propias de spaCR en una tabla que está en la lista de permitidas. Por ello, cada DELETE se restringe mediante :func:`measure_rows_clause`, que solo es verdadera para las filas que tienen un valor en una columna que el importador nunca escribió. Borrar un campo elimina las filas de measure de ese campo y deja las de la importación, en la misma tabla y en la misma sentencia.

records.context: "Present" means present in a row **measure wrote**. A table holding nothing but imported rows is left out of the "every table this run writes" set entirely, so it cannot make every field look partial either; it rejoins the moment measure puts a row in it. records.translation: "Present" significa presente en una fila **que escribió measure**. Las filas que una importación externa copió en una tabla canónica no cuentan: un proyecto construido exclusivamente por importación tiene ``cell`` como única tabla de campos y una fila en ella por cada campo, de modo que contarlas indicaría que toda la placa está medida, ``measure_crop`` no ejecutaría nada y los números importados pasarían por salida de spaCR. Una tabla que solo contiene filas importadas queda totalmente fuera del conjunto "every table this run writes", de modo que tampoco puede hacer que todos los campos parezcan parciales; vuelve a incorporarse en cuanto measure escribe una fila en ella. Véase :func:`measure_rows_clause`.

records.source: When resume *is* requested, in order:
records.translation: Cuando *sí* se solicita la reanudación, en orden:

records.context: 1. Read the previous processing session's settings out of the ``settings`` table in ``measurements.db`` and throw :class:`ResumeRefused` if anything material differs. **This must happen before** ``spacr.io._save_settings_to_db`` overwrites that table with the current settings — hence the placement of the call in ``measure_crop``. 2. Enumerate the fields in ``merged/`` and *validate* each one: a truncated ``.npy`` from a crash mid-``np.save`` is pending, not done, and is counted as rejected. 3. Ask the database which fields already have rows in **every** table the processing session writes. Fields with rows in only some tables are partial — a process killed between two inserts — and are re-queued. 4. Delete every row belonging to a pending field before it is executed again. This is what stops the resume from doubling rows. 5. Print the plan.
records.label: spacr.resume.plan_measure_resume#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context

Enumerate the fields in ``merged/`` and *validate* each one: a truncated ``.npy`` from a crash mid-``np.save`` is pending, not done, and is counted as rejected. 3. Ask the database which fields already have rows in **every** table the run writes. Fields with rows in only some tables are partial — a process killed between two inserts — and are re-queued. 4. Delete every row belonging to a pending field before it is re-run. This is what stops the resume from doubling rows. 5. Print the plan.

Lee la configuración de la ejecución anterior de la tabla ``settings`` de ``measurements.db`` y genera :class:`ResumeRefused` si algo relevante difiere. **Esto debe ocurrir antes de** que ``spacr.io._save_settings_to_db`` sobrescriba esa tabla con la configuración actual; de ahí la ubicación de la llamada en ``measure_crop``. 2. Enumera los campos de ``merged/`` y *valida* cada uno: un ``.npy`` truncado por un fallo a mitad de ``np.save`` está pendiente, no hecho, y se cuenta como rechazado. 3. Pregunta a la base de datos qué campos tienen ya filas en **todas** las tablas que escribe la ejecución. Los campos con filas solo en algunas tablas son parciales (un proceso interrumpido entre dos inserciones) y se vuelven a poner en cola. 4. Borra todas las filas de un campo pendiente antes de volver a ejecutarlo. Esto es lo que impide que la reanudación duplique filas. 5. Imprime el plan.

records.context: Not every pair of runs *can* be compared. Different plates, a module one processing session never ran, a different spaCR version: :func:`comparability` says so in words, and :func:`compare_runs` refuses to produce the three tables rather than presenting a misleading one. A version difference is deliberately a warning and not a blocker — it does not stop the comparison, but it has to be on application view, because a Cellpose upgrade between two processing sessions can account for a count change on its own.
records.label: spacr.run_compare#6
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Not every pair of runs *can* be compared. Different plates, a module one run never ran, a different spaCR version: :func:`comparability` says so in words, and :func:`compare_runs` refuses to produce the three tables rather than presenting a misleading one. A version difference is deliberately a warning and not a blocker — it does not stop the comparison, but it has to be on screen, because a Cellpose upgrade between two runs can account for a count change on its own.
records.translation: No todos los pares de ejecuciones *pueden* compararse. Placas distintas, un módulo que una ejecución nunca ejecutó, otra versión de spaCR: :func:`comparability` lo indica con palabras, y :func:`compare_runs` se niega a producir las tres tablas en lugar de presentar una engañosa. Una diferencia de versión es deliberadamente una advertencia y no un bloqueo (no detiene la comparación, pero tiene que estar en pantalla), porque una actualización de Cellpose entre dos ejecuciones puede explicar por sí sola un cambio en los recuentos.

records.source: The rank is defined here, once, so both sides of a diff are ranked the same way: rows are sorted by **descending absolute score**, ties broken by key. Absolute, because a screen's strongest hit is its largest effect in either direction and ranking a strong protective hit below a weak sensitising one would report rank churn that is an artefact of the sort. When no score column can be found the file's own row order is kept and :attr:`HitList.score_column` is empty, so a caller can tell a real ranking from a preserved one.
records.translation: La posición se define aquí, una sola vez, de modo que ambos lados de una diferencia se ordenan de la misma manera: las filas se ordenan por **puntuación absoluta descendente**, con los empates resueltos por clave. Absoluta, porque el acierto más fuerte de un cribado es su mayor efecto en cualquier dirección, y situar un acierto protector fuerte por debajo de uno sensibilizante débil notificaría una rotación de posiciones que es un artefacto de la ordenación. Cuando no se encuentra ninguna columna de puntuación, se conserva el orden de filas propio del archivo y :attr:`HitList.score_column` queda vacío, de modo que quien llama puede distinguir una ordenación real de una conservada.

records.context: spaCR has four views over the same measurement table — the UMAP, the plate heatmap, the database browser and the annotation grid. records.source: spaCR has four views over the same measurement table — the UMAP, the plate heatmap, the database browser and the annotation grid. This module holds the selection and filter state they share, so that a cluster lassoed in the UMAP can be located on the plate and a filter set in one view can narrow the others.
records.translation: spaCR tiene cuatro vistas sobre la misma tabla de mediciones: la UMAP, el mapa de calor de la placa, el explorador de la base de datos y la cuadrícula de anotación. Este módulo contiene el estado de selección y de filtro que comparten, de modo que un clúster rodeado con el lazo en la UMAP pueda localizarse en la placa y un filtro establecido en una vista pueda restringir las demás.

records.context: Conflating the two is the usual mistake. A filter can be re-applied to a different table (another plate, a re-run) and still mean something; a selection cannot, because it names individual objects.
records.label: spacr.selection#10
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Conflating the two is the usual mistake. A filter can be re-applied to a different table (another plate, a re-run) and still mean something; a selection cannot, because it names individual objects.
records.translation: Confundir ambas es el error habitual. Un filtro puede volver a aplicarse a otra tabla (otra placa, una nueva ejecución) y seguir significando algo; una selección no, porque nombra objetos individuales.

records.context: **A request** (:class:`ObjectRequest`) is neither: it is one act of routing. "Open exactly these twelve objects, because they are the cells this model called infected and the annotator called uninfected." A filter and a selection are *state* that every view reads; a request is an *event* that travels once, from the view that made it to the view that can show it. It carries the reason with it, because a view showing twelve extracted image regions out of ninety thousand has to be able to say why those twelve — otherwise they read as the whole dataset.
records.label: spacr.selection#11
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context

"Open exactly these twelve objects, because they are the cells this model called infected and the annotator called uninfected." A filter and a selection are *state* that every view reads; a request is an *event* that travels once, from the view that made it to the view that can show it. It carries the reason with it, because a view showing twelve crops out of ninety thousand has to be able to say why those twelve — otherwise they read as the whole dataset.
records.translation: **Una solicitud** (:class:`ObjectRequest`) no es ninguna de las dos: es un único acto de enrutamiento. "Open exactly these twelve objects, because they are the cells this model called infected and the annotator called uninfected." Un filtro y una selección son *estado* que lee cada vista; una solicitud es un *evento* que viaja una sola vez, desde la vista que la hizo hasta la vista que puede mostrarla. Lleva consigo el motivo, porque una vista que muestra doce recortes de noventa mil tiene que poder decir por qué esos doce; de lo contrario, parecen el conjunto de datos completo.

records.context: Objects are identified by :func:`object_keys` — the schema's own row identifier (``plateID``, ``rowID``, ``columnID``, ``fieldID``, ``object_label``), joined with the schema separator. records.source: Objects are identified by :func:`object_keys` — the schema's own row key (``plateID``, ``rowID``, ``columnID``, ``fieldID``, ``object_label``), joined with the schema separator. That is the one identity every table in ``measurements.db`` already agrees on, so a key from the UMAP means the same row in the plate view without a lookup table in between.
records.translation: Los objetos se identifican mediante :func:`object_keys`: la propia clave de fila del esquema (``plateID``, ``rowID``, ``columnID``, ``fieldID``, ``object_label``), unida con el separador del esquema. Esa es la única identidad en la que ya coinciden todas las tablas de ``measurements.db``, de modo que una clave de la UMAP designa la misma fila en la vista de la placa sin ninguna tabla de correspondencia intermedia.

records.context: **The object type is part of that identity.** Object tables are one type per table, so without the type a nucleus labelled 1 and a pathogen labelled 1 in the same microscope field of view compose to the *identical* structured-data name. A cell's own children are exactly the objects most likely to collide, which is where object linking is most useful — four objects would open as three extracted image regions, and which one you got would depend on the row order of ``png_list`` (:func:`spacr.active_learning.crops_for_object_keys` keeps the first). The type now goes into the object component of the structured-data name, exactly as :func:`spacr.schema.object_id` writes it
records.label: spacr.selection#14
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **The object type is part of that identity.** Object tables are one type per table, so without the type a nucleus labelled 1 and a pathogen labelled 1 in the same field compose to the *identical* key. A cell's own children are exactly the objects most likely to collide, which is where object linking is most useful — four objects would open as three crops, and which one you got would depend on the row order of ``png_list`` (:func:`spacr.active_learning.crops_for_object_keys` keeps the first). The type now goes into the object component of the key, exactly as :func:`spacr.schema.object_id` writes it
records.translation: **El tipo de objeto forma parte de esa identidad.** Las tablas de objetos tienen un tipo por tabla, de modo que, sin el tipo, un núcleo etiquetado como 1 y un patógeno etiquetado como 1 en el mismo campo componen la clave *idéntica*. Los hijos de una célula son precisamente los objetos con más probabilidad de colisionar, que es donde más útil resulta la vinculación de objetos: cuatro objetos se abrirían como tres recortes, y cuál se obtuviera dependería del orden de filas de ``png_list`` (:func:`spacr.active_learning.crops_for_object_keys` conserva el primero). Ahora el tipo entra en el componente de objeto de la clave, exactamente como lo escribe :func:`spacr.schema.object_id`

records.context: Two rules keep the change from breaking anything already written:
records.label: spacr.selection#16
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Two rules keep the change from breaking anything already written:
records.translation: Dos reglas evitan que el cambio rompa nada de lo ya escrito:

records.context: *Untyped keys do not move.* The untyped form is byte for byte what it was, so every key in every stored selection, exported ``.h5ad`` and prediction bundle still composes and parses as it did. There is nothing on disk to migrate.
records.label: spacr.selection#17
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: *Untyped keys do not move.* The untyped form is byte for byte what it was, so every key in every stored selection, exported ``.h5ad`` and prediction bundle still composes and parses as it did. There is nothing on disk to migrate.
records.translation: *Las claves sin tipo no cambian.* La forma sin tipo es byte a byte la misma que antes, de modo que todas las claves de todas las selecciones almacenadas, de los ``.h5ad`` exportados y de los paquetes de predicciones se siguen componiendo y analizando igual. No hay nada en disco que migrar.

records.context: *An untyped structured-data name is less specific, not wrong.* ``plate1_r1_c1_f1_7`` means "the object labelled 7 in that microscope field of view", which is exactly what it always meant — so it matches that object whatever its type, rather than silently matching one of them. Symmetrically a typed structured-data name still matches a row that has not said what it is. :meth:`Selection.mask_for` and :meth:`ObjectRequest.select_from` both apply that rule, and it is the whole migration: an old structured-data name is read as the thing it always said, never re-read as something narrower.
records.label: spacr.selection#18
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: *An untyped key is LESS SPECIFIC, not wrong.* ``plate1_r1_c1_f1_7`` means "the object labelled 7 in that field", which is exactly what it always meant — so it matches that object whatever its type, rather than silently matching one of them. Symmetrically a typed key still matches a row that has not said what it is. :meth:`Selection.mask_for` and :meth:`ObjectRequest.select_from` both apply that rule, and it is the whole migration: an old key is read as the thing it always said, never re-read as something narrower.
records.translation: *Una clave sin tipo es LESS SPECIFIC, no errónea.* ``plate1_r1_c1_f1_7`` significa "the object labelled 7 in that field", que es exactamente lo que siempre significó, de modo que coincide con ese objeto sea cual sea su tipo, en lugar de coincidir en silencio con uno de ellos. Simétricamente, una clave con tipo sigue coincidiendo con una fila que no ha indicado lo que es. :meth:`Selection.mask_for` y :meth:`ObjectRequest.select_from` aplican ambas esa regla, y esa es toda la migración: una clave antigua se interpreta como lo que siempre dijo, nunca se reinterpreta como algo más restringido.

records.source: A typed key is exactly the ``prcfo`` :func:`spacr.schema.compose_prcfo` writes for the same object, so the two identities converge as soon as the type is known. They differ only in the untyped case, where this joins the label bare and ``prcfo`` writes ``'o7'`` — kept that way on purpose, since changing it would move every key that already exists.
records.translation: Una clave con tipo es exactamente el ``prcfo`` que escribe :func:`spacr.schema.compose_prcfo` para el mismo objeto, de modo que ambas identidades convergen en cuanto se conoce el tipo. Solo difieren en el caso sin tipo, en el que esta función une la etiqueta sin prefijo y ``prcfo`` escribe ``'o7'``; se mantiene así a propósito, ya que cambiarlo movería todas las claves que ya existen.
